record.original_question: Does there exist a Banach space X such that the subspace K(X) of compact operators has property U in L(X), meaning that every functional on K(X) has a unique norm-preserving Hahn-Banach extension to L(X), even though K(X) is not an ideal in L(X)?

evidence.quote: Definition 11.1. (R. R. Phelps [4], 1960) The subspace Y has property U in X if every functional g ∈ Y∗ has a unique Hahn-Banch extension f ∈ X∗ (i.e. there is exactly one f ∈ X∗ satisfying f|Y = g and kfk = kgk).

Definition 11.2. (G. Godefroy, N.J. Kalton, P.D. Saphar [1], 1993) The subspace Y is an ideal in X if there exists a bounded linear projection P on X∗ such that kPk = 1 and kerP = Y⊥ := {f ∈ X∗ : f|Y = 0}.
Problem 11.5. Does there exist a Banach space X such that K(X) has property U in L(X) without being an ideal in L(X)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a (real or complex) Banach space, let $L(X)$ denote the Banach space of all bounded linear operators on $X$, and let $K(X) \subseteq L(X)$ denote the closed subspace of all compact operators on $X$.

Recall the following definitions for a closed subspace $Y$ of a Banach space $Z$:

(i) $Y$ has property U in $Z$ if every continuous linear functional $g \in Y^{*}$ admits exactly one Hahn–Banach extension to $Z$, i.e., there is a unique $f \in Z^{*}$ with $f|_{Y} = g$ and $\|f\| = \|g\|$.

(ii) $Y$ is an ideal in $Z$ if there exists a bounded linear projection $P: Z^{*} \to Z^{*}$ with $\|P\| = 1$ and $\ker P = Y^{\perp} = \{f \in Z^{*} : f|_{Y} = 0\}$.

It is known that being an ideal implies property U is not automatic, and conversely. The question is:

Does there exist a Banach space $X$ such that $K(X)$ has property U in $L(X)$ but $K(X)$ is not an ideal in $L(X)$?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a published resolution to the specific question of whether there exists a Banach space $X$ for which $K(X)$ has property U in $L(X)$ without being an ideal in $L(X)$. Related literature (Godefroy–Kalton–Saphar; works on ideals of compact operators and Hahn–Banach uniqueness) addresses adjacent questions, but no definitive answer was found, so the status is treated as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Ideals of compact operators
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses when K(X) is an ideal in L(X) in the sense of Godefroy–Kalton–Saphar.
status_evidence.claim: Related work treats the ideal property for K(X) in L(X) but does not resolve the property U vs. ideal distinction asked here.

status_evidence.title: Norm-attaining compact operators (M. Martín)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys properties of K(X) inside L(X) including Hahn–Banach smoothness and ideal structure.
status_evidence.claim: No statement found resolving Problem 11.5 about property U without K(X) being an ideal.
